candidates.title: How to do a kettlebell deadlift with proper form.
Beginner Kettlebell Exercise | The Kettlebell Deadlift
Exercise Tutorial: Kettlebell Deadlift
candidates.description:
The first exercise I will use to train the hinge movement pattern is the Kettlebell Deadlift, unless other variables hinder this movement. 

This exercise is a great way to learn how to deadlift properly. 

Common mistakes when doing this:
1. Starting off with the weight not between your heels. I like to use a line as a reference but if you don’t have lines on the ground to use, imagine a straight line and put the weight on that line between your heels. From experience, if you pick up the weight with the kettlebell in front of that “line,” let’s say it’s between your toes, if not properly engaged, it may put excess stress on your lower back. And continue to aim for that line each repetition as you go down and up. Train it right here before using a barbell, where the weight can’t be between your heels. 

2. Picking up the weight without creating tension in the body. Doing this may leave chance for your body to compensate in ways that don’t engage the right muscles. For example, having your arms bent to start. If your arms are bent when you start, you aren’t engaging your upper body (back) correctly, which can limit your ability do lift more and do it right. 

3. Looking forward when you start. Growing up I was taught to keep my eyes up, but if you watch the video, my eyes are set up so that my head is in line with the rest of my spine. I’m a fan of good lines and hyperextending your neck (looking up) in the bottom position “kinks” that straight line from your tailbone to your head. This can cause stress at your neck and may increase the risk of injury. 

4. Different parts of the body move separately as you go up and down. Oftentimes I might see someone doing this and either there upper body comes up first or their lower body. For example: you set up the lift, you start to pick it up and your torso comes up first and then the rest of the body. Or you set up to pick it up and your butt rises first before anything else. Regardless of which option that happens, everything isn’t moving together, and this leaves weak points in your body during the lift. Everything moves together.

#kettlebellexercises #deadlift #exercisetutorial
